children: is pursuing different strategies for the US and international markets as regulations, consumer preferences, and trade policies increasingly diverge across regions.
CEO Antonio Filosa said the US has become distinctly different from other major automotive markets, particularly Europe. That divide presents a challenge for Stellantis
because the US is its biggest profit generator, requiring the automaker to develop vehicles specifically suited to American conditions.
is relying entirely on domestic engineering and product development. Outside the US, the company is using partnerships with other automakers, including Chinese manufacturers Leapmotor
and Dongfeng, to support its operations in markets such as Europe.
Filosa said those partnerships are not being used to develop vehicles for the US market.
The approach comes as Washington takes a tougher stance toward cooperation between American and Chinese automakers. The Trump administration has criticized Ford
over its European joint venture with China’s Geely
, arguing that such arrangements could help Chinese manufacturers expand globally, media sources reported.
has defended its partnerships as a way to respond to changes in the international auto industry and improve efficiency.
, the widening gap between regional markets is making a unified global strategy increasingly difficult, forcing the company to tailor development and partnerships to individual markets.

title: Stellantis changes global playbook as regional auto priorities diverge
